They all leave the triangles through E and F, which share the top at 1.00, while C scores 0.75 and D 0.25; the endpoints themselves score 0." width="100%"} Ordinary betweenness counts shortest paths between every pair of nodes. Subset betweenness (Brandes, 2008) only counts paths that start in `sources=` and end in `targets=`, so it answers a focused question: which nodes carry the traffic from *these* origins to *those* destinations? Examples are the junctions between residential areas and business districts, or the proteins linking a set of receptors to a set of transcription factors. "Shortest" follows `shortest_path()`: hops, or total weight on a weighted graph. Scaling follows NetworkX: raw values by default (halved on undirected graphs, since each path is seen from both ends), or divided by `(n - 1)(n - 2)` with `normalized=True`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [sources]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Starting nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. [targets]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Destination nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, divide by `(n - 1)(n - 2)`. Default is `False`, as in NetworkX. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to measure path length by edge weight. If `None` (default), follows the graph. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store scores in. If `None` (default), uses `"betweenness_centrality_subset"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the scores as a node attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping node IDs to scores. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node does not exist, or weights are used and one is negative. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~betweenness_centrality`) : Count paths between all pairs. [](`~edge_betweenness_centrality_subset`) : The same measure for edges. ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a path A-B-C-D-E, traffic from A to C only passes through B, so D gets no credit: ::: {#1331049a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E")] ) ( path.betweenness_centrality_subset(["A"], ["C"]) .get_node_df() .select("label", "betweenness_centrality_subset") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

"D"0.0
"E"0.0
``` ::: ::: On the metro, the fastest trips from the Airport to Docks and to Shipyard both run through Business Park, Eastfield, Market, Riverside and Harbor, so those five stations, and no others, score. On an undirected graph, each trip adds `0.5`: ::: {#46705fbc .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl metro = ec.metro().betweenness_centrality_subset( ["Airport"], ["Docks", "Shipyard"] ) ( metro.get_node_df() .filter(pl.col("betweenness_centrality_subset") > 0) .select("label", "betweenness_centrality_subset") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
